title: Sarvesh Kushare Wins India's First CWG High Jump Silver After Injured Tejaswin Shankar's Selfless Assist
excerpt: Kushare cleared 2.25 metres to claim silver in Glasgow, while the defending champion Shankar competed through injury to provide crucial in-competition coaching.
body:
• Sarvesh Kushare won silver in the men's high jump at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, clearing 2.25 metres — India's first CWG medal in the event.
  • Jamaica's Romaine Beckford took gold, while defending champion Tejaswin Shankar competed through injury and provided in-competition coaching to Kushare throughout the final.
  • Shankar, who won gold at Birmingham 2022, reportedly put aside his own pain to guide Kushare through approach adjustments and bar strategy during the competition.
  • The result extends India's strong showing at Glasgow, where the athletics contingent entered the Games with three high jumpers eyeing medals.

A Silver and a Story

The men's high jump final at Glasgow's Hampden Park on Sunday produced a result that will be remembered not just for the medal, but for the moment of selflessness that made it possible.

Sarvesh Kushare cleared 2.25 metres to claim silver — India's first-ever Commonwealth Games medal in the men's high jump. Jamaica's Romaine Beckford won gold. But the story that captivated the stadium was what happened alongside the competition bar.

"https://x.com/ANI/status/2081855799232717079 Sarvesh Kushare cleared 2.25 metres to claim silver — India's first-ever Commonwealth Games medal in the men's high jump."

Tejaswin Shankar, India's defending champion who won gold at Birmingham 2022, arrived in Glasgow carrying an injury that severely limited his chances of repeating. Rather than withdraw, Shankar competed — and spent much of the final providing real-time coaching to his younger teammate.

The Defending Champion Turns Coach

Shankar, 26, is familiar to Indian-Americans as a former University of Kansas athlete who became the first Indian to win a CWG athletics gold. His leap of 2.22 metres in Birmingham made him an overnight star in Indian athletics circles.

In Glasgow, the roles reversed. With his own body unable to deliver peak performance, Shankar turned his experience and technical eye to Kushare's benefit. Witnesses at the venue described Shankar offering advice on approach runs, take-off positioning, and bar strategy between attempts — the kind of in-competition guidance that is rare even between teammates.

India had entered the high jump with three athletes and realistic medal hopes. The Athletics Federation of India identified the event as a target discipline after Kushare's rapid improvement over the past two seasons, during which he pushed his personal best above 2.25 metres in domestic and continental competitions.

Kushare's Rise

Kushare, a quieter presence in Indian athletics than the charismatic Shankar, has built his trajectory on consistency. His clearance of 2.25 metres in the final matched his season-best form and held up against a strong field that included jumpers from Jamaica, Australia, and the Bahamas.

Silver at a Commonwealth Games puts Kushare firmly in the conversation for India's 2028 Los Angeles Olympic team. The high jump has historically been one of India's weaker athletics disciplines — before Shankar's breakthrough in 2022, the country had never produced a serious contender at the international level. Two medals in consecutive CWG cycles suggests the investment in the event is paying off.

India's Athletics Campaign

The high jump silver adds to India's growing medal haul at Glasgow 2026, where the contingent has already delivered across weightlifting, boxing, and para athletics. The athletics programme entered the Games with cautious optimism, and Kushare's performance has validated that confidence.

For Shankar, the Games may have been bittersweet — an injury-compromised competition that fell short of his own standards. But his decision to turn the final into a coaching clinic for a younger athlete offered something arguably more valuable than another personal medal: a blueprint for how Indian athletics might sustain its CWG momentum beyond a single generation of talent.
